newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BNZ sees weaker H2, yr result still strong.
newsitem.headline: BNZ sees weaker H2, yr result still strong.

text.p: Bank of New Zealand managing director Gordon Wheaton said on Thursday the bank expected the "intensely competitive" nature of financial services to continue, and that business conditions would remain tough.

"While we expect to show a strong end-of-year result, the half year we are now in is not looking like producing the same level of financial result we've enjoyed for the March half," he said. BNZ is a unit of National Australian Bank.
BNZ reported a 30.2 percent rise in operating profit, after tax and minority interests, to NZ$194 million for the half year to March 31, 1997.
Its underlying profit, excluding interest recoveries and before debt provisioning, non-debt provisioning and tax, rose 10.7 percent to $209 million.

Wheaton said the outlook for the second half year meant the bank would have to put more emphasis on the quality of the business it attracted, rather than simply pursuing new customers in an effort to lift sales volumes.
Looking further ahead, however, Wheaton said there were indications that business conditions could improve.

Wheaton said demand for lending was likely to be promoted by a number of factors, including the recent fall in short term interest rates, strong growth among New Zealand's trading partners, and the absence of the rapid exchange rate rises seen in 1996.
"We expect that higher government spending will also assist growth in the economy and downstream business credit demand," Wheaton said.
He said despite the recent economic slowdown, BNZ believed inflationary risks remained and were likely to increase as growth improved.
